title: Legacy UFO program secrecy rooted in the Manhattan Project and the 1954 Atomic Energy Act

tellings.quote: specifically legacy programs starting with the same secrecy mechanisms as the Manhattan project and the 1954 atomic energy agreement birthing a lot of the secrecy behind uh UFO legacy program classification and controls.
SEC. 141. POLICY.—It shall be the policy of the Commission to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security.

r. The term 'Restricted Data' means all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to section 142.

plain: The claim is that the secret government UFO programs, which the tellers call legacy programs, were built on the same secrecy rules as the wartime project that made the atomic bomb, and on a 1954 atomic energy law. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb online tells Michels this. He draws on the former intelligence official David Grusch and on Grusch's interview with the broadcaster Joe Rogan. He says those programs began with 'the same secrecy mechanisms as the Manhattan project', with the 1954 atomic energy law 'birthing a lot of the secrecy behind uh UFO legacy program classification and controls'. If he is right, the way UFO secrets are kept would come straight out of the nuclear secrecy system. The other voice is the law itself, the Atomic Energy Act passed by Congress on 30 August 1954. UAPGerb does not say which part he means. If he means its secrecy rules, the act defines 'Restricted Data' as 'all data concerning' the 'design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons', the making of nuclear material, and its use for energy. It makes it the policy of the Atomic Energy Commission 'to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data' for 'the common defense and security'. That sets up a secrecy system built for atomic data. That UFO program secrecy grew out of it is UAPGerb's step, which the act neither states nor rules out.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which part of the 1954 act he means; if it is its secrecy rules, the act defines Restricted Data as "all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy" and makes it the Commission's policy "to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security", a secrecy regime built for atomic data. That the classification and controls of UFO legacy programs grew from that regime is the teller's step, which the act neither states nor excludes.
